Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important run chase. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of England. It will be the duo of Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Jamie Overton will get proceedings underway with the ball for England. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Sri Lanka's Lacklustre Bowling - There is not much to say about Sri Lanka's bowling effort, because after reducing England to 40/2 in the first 11 overs, they simply ran out of answers. The spinners were far from effective, and that was coupled with some sloppy work in the field. Apart from Wellalage, no bowler who delivered more than three overs managed to keep an economy rate under five, and the death-overs execution was far from ideal as well. Hasaranga, DDS and Vandersay picked up a wicket each, but Sri Lanka needed a lot more in this series decider. Now the onus is on their batters, who face an uphill task. Seeing England's performance, they will still believe they can match it, but it is certainly not going to be easy. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Root-Bethell-Brook Show - The openers could not do much, with Rehan Ahmed getting a start but failing to capitalise. After his dismissal, the innings slowed briefly as Root and Bethell took time to assess the conditions, but their constant strike rotation ensured the pressure stayed on the hosts. Once they found their rhythm, the runs flowed freely. The pair added 126 runs, both reaching their half-centuries, before Bethell fell short of a bigger score. Brook then walked in and lifted the tempo immediately, while Root held one end to bring up his 19th ODI century. Together they piled on 191 runs, including 88 runs in the last 5 overs. Brook went on to score a magnificent unbeaten 136 off just 66 balls, his career-best in ODIs.

England Produce Batting Masterclass - This has been one of the finest batting displays by a visiting side in sub-continent conditions. Harry Brook had labelled the surface in the previous game as the 'worst pitch', but if England can produce a performance like this on a wicket they found uncomfortable, the rest of the world should be on high alert about what they might do on a true batting track. Sri Lanka looked flat-footed and short of answers throughout, as England piled on their highest-ever ODI total in Sri Lankan conditions.

PITCH REPORT - Former English pacer, Steve Harmison, says that the pitch being used today is the one from the first ODI. Reckons that there are a few cracks and it will be slow and take some spin. Talks about the dimensions and says that it is 75 metres on one side of the square and 68 metres on the other. Feels that sweeping will be essential against the spinners and if England get a total of around 270, it will be very difficult to chase down.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka, says that they would have batted first as well but it is what it is. Informs that Wanindu Hasaranga is back in for Pramod Madushan. Adds that they were slightly below par with both bat and ball last time and they just want to start fresh and do the basics right. Mentions that running between the wickets is an issue but they would like for someone to play a long and anchoring knock.

Skipper of England, Harry Brook, says that the track looks very good for the batters, and they will try to put the maximum score on the board and defend it in the second inning. Further, he adds that it would be a high-scoring match as the pitch will hardly offer any turn on the ball. Continues that he would go with the same team, and he would like his spinners to attack the stumps. The batters should be able to make use of the pitch condition. Ended up saying that it's not easy to score runs, but they have to try to be a little funky.

We might also see Wanindu Hasaranga return to the Lankan lineup after missing the first two games, whereas for England, Zak Crawley might not feature yet again as he is still out injured. The battle lines are drawn and we are just a few minutes away from the toss. Stay tuned.

England have shown resilience in adapting to Asian conditions and also broke the 11-match away losing streak with their five-wicket victory in the second ODI. Joe Root has been the standout performer for the visitors, leading the series run-scoring with 136 runs, including a series-leveling 75 in the second match. Ben Duckett has also been consistent, tallying 101 runs across the first two games with a top score of 62. On the bowling front, veteran leg-spinner Adil Rashid remains the focal point of the attack, while Jamie Overton has provided valuable support with a recent two-wicket haul.

Sri Lanka enter this final match after a mixed performance on home soil, winning the opener by 19 runs before failing to defend a modest total in the second game. In the first ODI, they successfully defended 271, largely thanks to Kusal Mendis, who anchored the innings with a brilliant unbeaten 93. Their bowling attack, led by the spin duo of Jeffrey Vandersay and Dunith Wellalage, has been their primary strength. Dunith delivered a match-winning all-round performance in the first game with 2 wickets and three catches, while Vandersay has consistently led the wicket-taking charts. However, the hosts struggled with the bat in the second game, being dismissed for 219 despite useful contributions from Charith Asalanka and Dhananjaya de Silva, and they will be eager to make amends

The three-match ODI series between England and Sri Lanka reaches its climax at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo. This third and final match serves as a critical series decider, with both teams currently leveled at 1-1 after two closely contested matches. Beyond the trophy, the fixture holds significant weight for the ICC rankings, as both nations aim to maintain their positions within the top eight to ensure automatic qualification for the 2027 World Cup. On that note, welcome to the coverage.

All set for a thrilling finale! The stage is set for a thrilling finale as England and Sri Lanka face off in the third and final ODI at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo. With the series locked at 1-1, this match is a winner-takes-all contest. Both teams have shown they can win in these conditions, making this decider highly anticipated. Fans can expect a tense battle on a pitch that has heavily favored spin bowlers throughout the series. Sri Lanka had an early lead in the series - The series opener saw the hosts draw first blood with a hard-fought 19-run victory. Sri Lanka posted a competitive 271/6, thanks largely to a brilliant 92 from Kusal Mendis and a late cameo by Dunith Wellalage. In reply, England looked comfortable at one stage with Ben Duckett and Joe Root scoring half-centuries, but the Sri Lankan spinners choked the run flow in the middle overs. The visitors eventually crumbled under pressure, falling short as the local spinners exploited the turning track perfectly. England bounced back impressively - In the second game, England bounced back to level the series with a comfortable 5-wicket win. Learning from their previous mistakes, the English bowlers restricted Sri Lanka to a modest 219, with spinners Adil Rashid and part-timer Joe Root doing the damage. Root then starred with the bat, anchoring the chase with a classy 75 not out. His composure, combined with Harry Brook's steady innings, ensured England crossed the line calmly, setting up this final showdown. Toss is Crucial! Yes, for this final clash, the toss could be crucial, as the Colombo pitch is expected to turn. Sri Lanka will rely heavily on their spin attack to unsettle the English lineup again, while England will look to Joe Root and their top order to navigate the challenge. It will be a test of temperament as much as skill. Whoever handles the pressure better in the turning conditions will likely lift the trophy.
